newsitem.title: UK: Gold OTC option market lacklustre as vols drop off.
newsitem.headline: Gold OTC option market lacklustre as vols drop off.

text.p: OTC gold options have lost some of their recent dazzle with nearby volatilities dropping off and business thinning, dealers said on Wednesday.
Recent business in options has been generally featureless ahead of next week's expiry of March options.
"Nothing too exciting is happening. We've seen just bits and pieces of options business over the past few days, with $345-$360 as the range and most interest in April to June dates," a dealer said.
The market remained jittery and undecided about gold's next move.
"I suppose there has been more interest in calls at $355 than puts at $345," the dealer said.
But another dealer said low deltas were in vogue with interest in $340 strikes emerging. Another said puts as low as $330 had been sold recently.
"People are still keen to pay a little more for puts because they're nervous of a drop in gold. they remember that at the start of the year gold dropped from $345 to $335," he added.
For next Tuesday's expiry, open interest was thought to lie on every dollar strike within gold's recent trading range, dealers said.
However, the psychological $350 strike level was still expected to dominate options strategies unless the underlying price managed to break above it before the expiry.
As the price of spot gold started levelling off some 10 days ago, nearby volatilities have also dropped and remained under pressure this week, dealers said.
One-month at the money implied volatilities were bid at around 10.5 percent, a sharp decline from as high as 14.5 around two weeks ago.
Three month volatilies were bid at 8.7 to nine percent, while six-month vols were bid at around 7.5 percent.
Spot gold, meanwhile, was trading in a narrow range on Wednesday between $350 and $348 an ounce, fixing at $349.10 in the afternoon.
"With volatilities down, it's slowed to the pace of a normal, busy market. But it certainly slower than at the start of the year," a trader said.
But there was no sign yet that nearby volatilities would continue sinking to last year's lows around four percent.
